clue.text: A cent, so worthless, put at back of the wallet

indicators.note: something worthless is no good and falls apart, so the letters of a cent so are broken up and rebuilt

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter, here the last of the word the

explanation.surface: Someone tucking a cent into the back of their wallet, though it is worth almost nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worthless' looks like a comment on the cent but rearranges ACENTSO into NOTECAS; 'back of the' adds E at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: an old-fashioned word for a pocketbook that holds banknotes.

clue.text: Shopper hurried up, before bank's closure

definitions.note: a shopper is someone who shops, that is informs on, others to the police

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is written from bottom to top

parts.note: hurried means ran

indicators.note: a word's closure is its final letter, here the end of bank

explanation.surface: A customer rushes to the bank before it shuts for the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shopper' looks like a customer, but in British slang to shop someone is to betray them; 'up' turns RAN into NAR in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang synonym: a police informer, someone who grasses on associates.

clue.text: Examiner keeps scripture marks for a term at Harvard

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it inside, so the examiner word wraps round the other pieces

parts.note: an examiner is a tester
RI, religious instruction, the school subject of scripture
M is the abbreviation for mark, as in Deutschmark

explanation.surface: An examiner holds on to the marks for a scripture paper during a term at an American university.
explanation.walkthrough: RI is religious instruction, the British school subject. Many US colleges divide the year into three terms.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: an American academic year split in three uses this word for each of its terms.

clue.text: Islander's extremely canny, quietly leading rebellion

definitions.note: read as islander is, a person from an island

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes, the outer letters of canny

parts.note: P, piano, the musical direction for quietly
a riot is a rebellion

explanation.surface: An islander, shrewd and soft-spoken, heads an uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'Islander's' stands for 'is', linking definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a native of Cyprus, a Mediterranean island.

clue.text: It gets hot overnight: heart rate goes wonky

indicators.note: something wonky is skewed and unsteady, so the letters of heart rate goes are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone's pulse turns erratic in the night as they overheat.
explanation.walkthrough: A storage heater is a British appliance that charges up on cheap overnight electricity and releases heat in the day.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: the appliance warms its bricks during the night on off-peak power.

clue.text: Prophet and priest rejected religious pilgrimage

parts.note: Eli is the priest in the Book of Samuel who raised Samuel

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the pilgrimage word is read in reverse

parts.note: the haj is the Muslim pilgrimage to Mecca

explanation.surface: A prophet and a priest turn down a holy journey.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: an Old Testament prophet of Israel, taken up to heaven in a whirlwind.

clue.text: Hollywood swindle going on and on?

parts.note: Hollywood is in Los Angeles, LA
a sting is a confidence trick or swindle

explanation.surface: A Hollywood con that seems to run forever.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: enduring, continuing for a long time.

clue.text: Oliver perhaps, first person to entertain friend in France

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to take them in, so the French pronoun holds the friend

parts.note: je is the French first person pronoun, I, with in France applying to both pieces
ami is French for friend

explanation.surface: Oliver, say, is the first to host a French friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in France' covers both JE and AMI. Jamie Oliver is a British TV chef.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the celebrity cook's first name, with 'perhaps' showing one instance.

clue.text: Lack of certainty, say, in the Conservative leader, wavering

indicators.note: wavering means unsteady, so these letters wobble into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here of Conservative

explanation.surface: Doubt, so to speak, inside the Tory leader who keeps wavering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wavering' looks like a description of the leader but rearranges SAYINTHE plus C.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: reluctance or indecision born of doubt.

clue.text: Charge about home getting part of house safe from storms

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the charge word goes round the home word

parts.note: a rap is a criminal charge
at home is in
the roof is part of a house

explanation.surface: A charge for home improvements that make part of the house weatherproof.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: impervious to rain and so protected in bad weather.

clue.text: Troops wield power, with a great number chasing foe endlessly

indicators.note: chasing means coming after, so the other pieces follow the shortened foe
without its end, the word foe loses its last letter

parts.note: to reign is to wield power
a legion is a great number

explanation.surface: Soldiers exercise power, a vast army pursuing an enemy without end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Troops' is the definition, and 'chasing' is an order signal: the later pieces come behind, not a pursuit.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the French military corps of foreign volunteers is a body of troops.

clue.text: Greek island, second to be captured by special troops

indicators.note: captured by means held inside, so the special forces word surrounds the second word

parts.note: the SAS, Special Air Service, are British special forces
a mo is a moment, a second

explanation.surface: A Greek island about to fall to special forces.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: an Aegean island, birthplace of Pythagoras.

clue.text: Part of North African town in area near sea

indicators.note: near means next to, placing the sea word beside the others

parts.note: the Med is the Mediterranean Sea

explanation.surface: A district of a North African town located by the coast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'near' sets MED beside IN and A.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the old walled quarter of a North African city.

clue.text: End tucked in torn clothing

indicators.note: tucked in means placed inside, so the end word sits within the torn word

parts.note: rent means torn
an end is an aim or goal

explanation.surface: A loose end is tucked into ripped clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'End' means a purpose, not a tip.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an archaic, literary word for garments.

clue.text: Thus identifies thief top gunner's shot

indicators.note: shot means ruined or broken, so the letters of thief top gunner's are rearranged

explanation.surface: A shot from a top gunman thereby identifies the thief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' looks like gunfire but signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to name or inform on someone as the guilty party.

clue.text: Old soldier moved quietly into jetty

indicators.note: into means placed inside, so the moving word goes inside the jetty word

parts.note: a pier is a jetty
stole means crept or moved quietly

explanation.surface: A veteran creeps onto a jetty.
explanation.definitionFit: Historical term: a soldier armed with a handgun.

clue.text: Limit alcoholic drink — here's why?

parts.note: to ration is to limit
ale is beer

explanation.surface: Someone asks why they should cut back on booze.
explanation.definitionFit: Paraphrase: the reasoning behind something, offered to explain a choice.

clue.text: Arranged nice drives: attempt to back US tourism, perhaps

indicators.note: to back means to come behind, so the attempt word follows US
arranged means put in order, so the letters of nice drives are reorganised

parts.note: taken as written
a try is an attempt

explanation.surface: Pleasant drives laid on as a bid to boost American tourism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to back' reads as supporting America, but here it means coming behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: tourism is a sector that provides services rather than goods.

clue.text: Noticed team-mate swallowing cold drink

indicators.note: the words Noticed team-mate swallow and so contain the answer within them

explanation.surface: Someone spots a teammate gulping a chilled drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a chilled beverage of tea served with ice.

clue.text: Unionist forces in revolts

parts.note: prises means forces, as in levering open

explanation.surface: Unionist troops become involved in rebellions.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: insurrections, risings against authority.

clue.text: Old Welshman rolling after drinking half of best rum

indicators.note: drinking means taking in, so the Welshman word holds the part of best
rolling means turning over, so the Welshman word is read backwards

parts.note: Taff is a nickname for a Welshman

indicators.note: half of best is its first two letters

explanation.surface: An old Welshman staggers after downing half his best rum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rolling' reverses the Welshman to FFAT. 'rum' looks like the spirit but is the British adjective meaning odd.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: rum in its British sense of strange or unconventional.

clue.text: Fellow linguist half abandoned illicit relationship

indicators.note: with half dropped, only the first four of linguist's eight letters remain

explanation.surface: A colleague who studies languages has half given up on a secret affair.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a brief affair, often outside a committed relationship.

clue.text: Firmly fix eastern and northern itinerary during discussion

indicators.note: in discussion means spoken out, so the itinerary word is heard rather than written

parts.note: a route is an itinerary

explanation.surface: Settling a route through the east and north while talking it over.
explanation.walkthrough: In British pronunciation route sounds like root.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to establish deeply, as a plant takes hold in soil.

clue.text: Where officers eat pickle?

definitions.meaning: a military dining room for officers
a pickle is a predicament or muddle

explanation.surface: Pickle on the menu where officers dine.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: the military dining hall and a state of confusion.

clue.text: Order not entirely predictable

indicators.note: not entirely means only part of the word predictable is used

explanation.surface: An instruction that is only partly foreseeable.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an official decree or command.

clue.text: Restore control, say

parts.note: to rein in is to control; a rein is a control
to say is to state

explanation.surface: An instruction to regain command, so to speak.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to bring back into a former position.

clue.text: Tease lecturer having a new coat

parts.note: to rag is to tease

explanation.surface: Mocking a lecturer for wearing a new coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having' is a link joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: an overcoat whose sleeves run up to the collar, named after Lord Raglan.

clue.text: Frank initially mislaid old records for dances

indicators.note: the initial letter is mislaid, so the frank word loses its first letter

parts.note: frank means honest
EPs, extended-play discs, are old records

explanation.surface: Frank first lost some vintage records of dance music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' looks like a name but is the adjective meaning candid.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: ballroom dances of the early twentieth century in quick march time.
